title: Remote calls: timeouts, retries, and unknown outcomes
outcome: Bound dependency work and design retries around a logical command rather than an exception name.
useCase: Email, payments, file conversion, and third-party APIs.
benefits: Contained failure and explainable retry behavior.
drawbacks: Some outcomes remain ambiguous without provider support.
cue: Bound the wait. Identify the command. Admit uncertainty.

trace.title: Saved intent
trace.detail: A remote call crosses a failure boundary. The provider can reject, respond slowly, complete and lose the response, or return malformed data. A timeout says you did not get an answer in time; it does not prove no side effect occurred.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Business change commits with a receipt intent. A worker sends it with eventKey E. The provider accepts E but the response is lost. A retry uses E again under the provider’s documented key contract, or reconciliation resolves uncertainty when such a contract is absent.

Do not retry an entire use case if that repeats unrelated writes. Put the retry around the boundary you actually intend to repeat.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Nested retries multiply attempts. A 3-attempt client inside a 3-attempt job can make nine calls. A fallback that reports success without performing the required effect is a false result.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Bound dependency work and design retries around a logical command rather than an exception name. Explain one example and one failure.
